message:
## Vulnerability Digest

This DLL component scan used only `DLL_software_component.txt`; obvious aliases, repeated rows, and version variants were consolidated. The scan window was **2026-10-10 07:40 UTC through 2026-10-11 07:40 UTC** (**2026-10-10 13:10 IST through 2026-10-11 13:10 IST**).

No confirmed new vulnerability was found that both falls within the strict 24-hour window and maps directly to a component in the DLL inventory. The newest reviewed NuGet advisories predated the cutoff, and candidate vendor/security pages either contained older disclosures or did not identify an in-window issue affecting a listed component. Sources checked included the [GitHub Advisory Database for NuGet](https://github.com/advisories?query=ecosystem%3Anuget), [GitHub Advisory Database for npm](https://github.com/advisories?query=ecosystem%3Anpm), and relevant vendor security pages.

### MongoDB ecosystem verification

The mandatory dedicated sweep covered MongoDB Server Community and Enterprise, `mongod`, `mongos`, Atlas and Atlas services, Ops Manager, Cloud Manager, Compass, `mongosh`, Database Tools, Kubernetes Operator, official drivers and connectors, BI Connector, Charts, Realm/App Services, and official MongoDB libraries and integrations.

No MongoDB-family vulnerability could be verified as newly reported in the scan window. Recent search results, including Ops Manager 9.0.1 (released October 5) and older server, driver, shell, SQL-interface, and Search/Vector Search security fixes, were outside the window and were not recast as new findings. Sources: [MongoDB Ops Manager changelog](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/ops-manager/current/release-notes/application/), [MongoDB Server release notes](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/release-notes/8.2/), [MongoDB C Driver release notes](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/languages/c/c-driver/current/reference/release-notes/), and [CISA](https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog).

### Review priority

No immediate review is recommended based on newly reported, in-scope vulnerabilities during this window. Continue normal monitoring; this conclusion does not assess older vulnerabilities already associated with the listed legacy component versions.
